title: Theorem
head: environment

label: q:KSX-local-entropy
title: Question
head: environment

label: thm:intro-covariance
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:intro-covariance}
If $0\ne S\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{TT}}$ satisfies $\Delta S=\lambda S$, then
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_0(S^\vee,S^\vee)=\kappa_n(\lambda)
       \|S^\vee\|_{L^2(SM,m_0)}^2,
\]
where
\begin{equation*}
 \kappa_n(\lambda)=\frac{J(a+\mu)J(a-\mu)}{J(n+3)},
 \qquad a=\frac{n+3}{2},
\end{equation*}
and
\[
 J(z)=\sqrt\pi\,\frac{\Gamma(z/2)}{\Gamma((z+1)/2)},\qquad
 \mu^2=\frac{(n-1)^2+8}{4}-\lambda.
\]
We choose $\mu\geq0$ when $\mu^2\geq0$, and $\mu$ with positive
imaginary part otherwise; the formula is unchanged by $\mu\mapsto-\mu$.
head: environment

label: hd:main
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: cor:local-entropy-curves
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:local-entropy-curves}
Let $(M^3,g_0)$ be a closed hyperbolic three-manifold. There is a
$C^\infty$ neighborhood $\mathcal U$ of $g_0$ such that every smooth
metric $g\in\mathcal U$ satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{Sc}_g\geq-6\quad\Longrightarrow\quad h(g)\leq2.
\]
Equality holds if and only if $g=\varphi^*g_0$ for a diffeomorphism
$\varphi$ of $M$.
head: environment

label: hd:saddle-intro
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{hd:saddle-intro}
If $n\geq4$ and $(M,g_0)$ admits a nonzero trace-free Codazzi tensor,
then $g_0$ is a saddle to second order on
$\mathcal M_{-n(n-1)}$ modulo diffeomorphisms. There are smooth curves
$g_s^+,g_s^-$ in this space through $g_0$ for which, for sufficiently
small nonzero $s$,
\[
 h(g_s^+)>n-1,\qquad h(g_s^-)<n-1.
\]
Such closed hyperbolic manifolds exist in every dimension $n\geq4$.
The curves converge smoothly to $g_0$ as $s\to0$.
head: environment

label: prop:flaminio
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:flaminio}
Let $\widehat g_s$ be a $C^2$ curve of $C^5$ negatively curved metrics
such that $\operatorname{Vol}(M,\widehat g_s)=V_0$, $\widehat g_0=g_0$, and
$\dot{\widehat g}_0=S$.  Then
\begin{equation*}
 \left.\frac{d^2}{ds^2}\right|_0 h(\widehat g_s)
 =\operatorname{Cov}_0\left(T(S)^\vee,\frac{n-1}{2}S^\vee\right),
\end{equation*}
where
\[
T(S)=\frac14 \nabla^*\nabla S-\frac12\delta^*\delta S+\frac12(\operatorname{tr}_{g_0}S)g_0-\frac12 S.
\]
In particular, $T(S)=\tfrac14PS$ for $S\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{TT}}$, where
$P=\Delta-2$.
head: environment

label: lem:integrability
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:integrability}
For every $S\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{TT}}$ there is a smooth curve
$g_s\in\mathcal M_{-n(n-1)}$ with $g_{s=0}=g_0$ and
$\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}g_s=S$.
For sufficiently small $s$, the metrics $g_s$ remain negatively curved.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $k\geq4$ and $0<\alpha<1$. On the open neighborhood of $(0,0)$
where $g_0+sS+ug_0$ is positive definite, consider
\[
 \Phi(s,u):=\operatorname{Sc}(g_0+sS+u g_0)+n(n-1),
 \qquad
 \Phi:\mathbb R\times C^{k,\alpha}(M)
       \longrightarrow C^{k-2,\alpha}(M).
\]
For $h=fg_0$ one has $\operatorname{tr} h=nf$ and $\delta h=-df$.
Equation \eqref{eq:scalar-linearization-hyperbolic} therefore gives
\begin{equation*}
 D_u\Phi(0,0)f
 =D\operatorname{Sc}_{g_0}(fg_0)
 =(n-1)(\nabla^*\nabla+n)f.
\end{equation*}
The operator on the right is an isomorphism
$C^{k,\alpha}\to C^{k-2,\alpha}$ because it is elliptic, self-adjoint,
and strictly positive.  The implicit function theorem produces a curve
$u(s)$ with $u(0)=0$ and $\Phi(s,u(s))=0$.  Since $S$ is TT,
\eqref{eq:scalar-linearization-hyperbolic} gives
$D_s\Phi(0,0)=0$; differentiating $\Phi(s,u(s))=0$ then shows
$\dot u(0)=0$.  Thus
\[
 g_s=g_0+sS+u(s)g_0
\]
has $\dot g_0=S$ and the required scalar curvature.  Elliptic regularity
and the smooth implicit function theorem give a smooth curve when $S$ is
smooth.  Finally, negative sectional curvature is open in the $C^2$
topology.
head: environment

label: hd:bochner
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The bundle-valued Bochner identity (see \cite{Besse}*{p.~355}) is
\[
 (d_\nabla d_\nabla^*+d_\nabla^*d_\nabla)S
 =\nabla^*\nabla S-R^\circ(S)+\operatorname{Ric}_{g_0}\circ S.
\]
Here $S$ is viewed as a $T^*M$-valued one-form. For trace-free
$S$ at curvature $-1$, the right-hand side is $\Delta S-nS$.
For $S\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{TT}}$, we also have $d_\nabla^*S=0$ and $d_\nabla S=C$.
With $|C|^2=\sum_{i,j,k}C_{ijk}^2$ in an orthonormal frame, the
bundle-valued two-form norm is
$\|d_\nabla S\|_{L^2}^2=\tfrac12\|C\|_{L^2}^2$,
so integration gives \eqref{hd:codazzi-energy}.
If $S$ is Codazzi, the same identity gives $\Delta S=nS$.
Conversely, equality in \eqref{hd:codazzi-energy} forces $C=0$.
Finally, contracting the Codazzi equation gives
$\nabla^iS_{ij}=\nabla_j\operatorname{tr} S$, so a trace-free Codazzi tensor is TT.
head: environment

label: thm:constrained-hessian
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Proposition~\ref{prop:flaminio} and $T(S)=\frac14PS$ give
\[
 \left.\frac{d^2}{ds^2}\right|_0h(\widehat g_s)
 =\frac{n-1}{8}\operatorname{Cov}_0\bigl((PS)^\vee,S^\vee\bigr).
\]
Multiplying \eqref{eq:volume-second} by
$-(n-1)/(nV_0)$ gives the second term of
\eqref{eq:main-hessian}.  This proves the formula and its independence of the chosen curve.
head: environment

label: thm:negative-directions
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
After compression to the TT space, the symmetrization of
$\Pi_2P$ is a pseudodifferential operator of order one.
The orthogonal TT projection has order zero and nonzero principal
symbol, as recalled in Section~\ref{sec:criterion}.  The second term of \eqref{eq:main-hessian} has principal symbol
\[
 -\frac{1}{4nV_0}|\xi|^2\operatorname{Id}
\]
on the TT symbol space.  It is therefore the principal symbol of the full
Hessian.  Standard elliptic spectral theory gives all three conclusions.

On a hyperbolic manifold, $\nabla^*\nabla$ preserves $\mathcal T_{\mathrm{TT}}$.  If
$\nabla^*\nabla S_j=\lambda_jS_j$ with $\lambda_j\to\infty$, the order
$-1$ property gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_0(S_j^\vee)
 =O(\lambda_j^{-1/2})\|S_j\|_{L^2(M)}^2.
\]
Substitution in \eqref{eq:main-hessian} shows that
$\mathcal H(S_j,S_j)<0$ for all sufficiently large $j$.
head: environment

label: hd:polar-laplace
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: hd:polar-div
title: Proof
body_md:
In this lifted frame, the connection formulas are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \nabla_{e_0}e_0&=0,&
 \nabla_{e_a}e_0=\nabla_{e_0}e_a&=\coth r\,e_a,\\
 \nabla_{e_a}e_b&=\nabla^\sigma_{e_a}e_b
 -\sinh r\cosh r\,\delta_{ab}e_0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Trace-freeness gives $\sum_aS(e_a,e_a)=-\sinh^2r\,U$.
Applying the connection formulas to $W$ therefore gives
\[
 \sum_a(\nabla_{e_a}S)(e_0,e_a)
 =\operatorname{div}_\sigma W+n\sinh r\cosh r\,U.
\]
Taking the trace in the hyperbolic orthonormal frame, the radial
component of $\delta S=0$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{hd:polar-div}
 \frac{\operatorname{div}_\sigma W}{\sinh^2r}
 =-\partial_rU-n\coth r\,U.
\end{equation}

To compute $(\Delta S)(e_0,e_0)$, first note that
\[
 (\nabla_{e_0}S)(e_0,e_0)=\partial_rU,\qquad
 (\nabla_{e_a}S)(e_0,e_0)=e_aU-2\coth r\,W_a.
\]
Differentiate once more at a point where the spherical frame is normal,
and take the trace in the hyperbolic orthonormal frame.  Each angular
term contributes a factor $(\sinh r)^{-2}$, giving
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 -(\Delta S)(e_0,e_0)
 &=\partial_r^2U+(n-1)\coth r\,\partial_rU
      -\frac{\Delta_\sigma U}{\sinh^2r}\\
 &\quad-\frac{4\coth r}{\sinh^2r}\operatorname{div}_\sigma W
      -2n\coth^2r\,U.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Substituting \eqref{hd:polar-div} and
$(\Delta S)(e_0,e_0)=\lambda U$ proves \eqref{hd:polar-equation}.
head: environment

label: pro:correlation
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $x\in M$ and abbreviate $F(t)=F_{x,A,S}(t)$.
The geodesic flow is smooth, so $F$ is smooth.  Replacing $\xi$ by
$-\xi$ changes $\gamma_{x,\xi}(t)$ to $\gamma_{x,\xi}(-t)$ and
reverses its velocity.  Since both tensor evaluations are quadratic,
this substitution gives $F(-t)=F(t)$ and hence $F'(0)=0$.

Set $Y_{A_x}(\xi)=A_x(\xi,\xi)$.  In the polar coordinates above,
\[
 F(r)=\int_{S_xM}Y_{A_x}(\xi)U(r,\xi)\,d\sigma_x(\xi).
\]
Since $A_x$ is trace-free, $Y_{A_x}$ is a spherical harmonic of
degree two and $\Delta_\sigma Y_{A_x}=2nY_{A_x}$.  Thus integration
by parts on the sphere gives
\[
 \int_{S_xM}Y_{A_x}\Delta_\sigma U\,d\sigma_x
 =\int_{S_xM}(\Delta_\sigma Y_{A_x})U\,d\sigma_x
 =2nF(r).
\]
Averaging \eqref{hd:polar-equation} against $Y_{A_x}$ and
differentiating under the integral in $r$ gives
\[
 F''+(n+3)\coth r\,F'
 +\left(\lambda+2n\coth^2r-\frac{2n}{\sinh^2r}\right)F=0.
\]
Since $\coth^2r-(\sinh r)^{-2}=1$, this is precisely the
differential equation in \eqref{hd:correlation-ode}.

Because $\coth r$ is singular at zero, we prove uniqueness among
smooth even solutions directly.
Put $c=\lambda+2n$ and $p(r)=(\sinh r)^{n+3}$.  A smooth solution
$f$ satisfies $(pf')'=-cpf$ and $p(r)f'(r)\to0$ as $r\downarrow0$.
Integrating twice gives
\[
 f(r)=f(0)-c(Kf)(r),\qquad
 (Kf)(r)=\int_0^r\frac{1}{p(u)}\int_0^u p(v)f(v)\,dv\,du.
\]
Monotonicity of $p$ gives the estimate
\[
 \|Kh\|_{C[0,\varepsilon]}
 \leq \frac{\varepsilon^2}{2}\|h\|_{C[0,\varepsilon]}.
\]
For $|c|\varepsilon^2/2<1$, the map $h\mapsto b-cKh$ is a
contraction.  Thus at most one smooth solution has initial value $b$.
For existence, the regular-singular
equation has indicial roots $0$ and $-(n+2)$.  Its regular branch
has a convergent even power series with arbitrary constant term $b$.  Continuation for the linear equation on $(0,\infty)$
and even reflection give the global solution; taking $b=1$
defines $\varphi_{n,\lambda}$.

By linearity, $F(0)\varphi_{n,\lambda}$ solves the same equation as
$F$ and has the same value at zero.  Uniqueness and evenness thus give
\begin{equation*}
 F_{x,A,S}(t)=\varphi_{n,\lambda}(t)F_{x,A,S}(0)
 \qquad(t\in\mathbb R).
\end{equation*}
Integrating over $x$ with measure
$dV_{g_0}/V_0$ proves \eqref{eq:correlation-factor}.
head: environment

label: thm:covariance-multiplier
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Substituting $u=\tanh r$ in \eqref{hd:spherical-integral} gives
\[
 \varphi_{n,\lambda}(t)=\frac{1}{J(2a)}
 \int_{\mathbb R}(\cosh r)^{-q_-}
                    (\cosh(r-t))^{-q_+}\,dr.
\]
We first justify absolute convergence of the time integral.
If $\mu$ is purely imaginary, $\Re q_\pm=a>0$.
If $\mu$ is real, $\lambda\geq n$ implies
$0\leq\mu\leq(n-3)/2=a-3$, so $q_\pm\geq3$.
Consequently, the substitution $s=r-t$ gives
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R^2}
 \left|(\cosh r)^{-q_-}(\cosh(r-t))^{-q_+}\right|\,dr\,dt
 =J(\Re q_-)J(\Re q_+)<\infty.
\]
Thus $\varphi_{n,\lambda}\in L^1(\mathbb R)$, and Fubini's theorem
gives
\begin{equation*}
 \int_{\mathbb R}\varphi_{n,\lambda}(t)\,dt
 =\frac{J(q_-)J(q_+)}{J(2a)}=\kappa_n(\lambda).
\end{equation*}
Both evaluation functions have zero mean. Combining
\eqref{eq:cov2} with Proposition~\ref{pro:correlation} yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Cov}_0(A^\vee,S^\vee)
 &=\int_{\mathbb R}\int_{SM}A^\vee(S^\vee\circ\phi_t)\,dm_0\,dt\\
 &=\left(\int_{\mathbb R}\varphi_{n,\lambda}(t)\,dt\right)
       \int_{SM}A^\vee S^\vee\,dm_0,
 \end{aligned}
\]
which proves the formula.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Insert \eqref{hd:covariance-final} and \eqref{hd:fiber} into
\eqref{eq:main-hessian} to obtain \eqref{hd:main-mode}.
The preceding comparisons determine the sign on every eigenspace.
By Section~\ref{sec:criterion}, there is an $L^2(M)$-orthonormal
TT eigenbasis $\{S_j\}$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_j\to\infty$.
Orthogonal eigenmodes have zero cross-covariance, so the Hessian is
diagonal in this basis.

For a smooth TT tensor $S=\sum_js_jS_j$, its partial sums converge
in every Sobolev norm, as do their images under $P$.
Continuity of covariance in a fixed H\"older norm permits passage
to the limit in \eqref{eq:main-hessian}. The resulting formula is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:full-spectral-hessian}
 \mathcal H(S,S)=\frac{1}{4n(n+2)V_0}
 \sum_j(\lambda_j-2)
 \bigl((n-1)\kappa_n(\lambda_j)-(n+2)\bigr)s_j^2.
\end{equation}
By \eqref{hd:high-frequency}, the coefficient of $s_j^2$ is
$-\lambda_j/(4nV_0)+O(\sqrt{\lambda_j})$.
In particular, its absolute value is bounded by $C(1+\lambda_j)$,
so the series converges absolutely and extends the Hessian
continuously to $H^1\cap\overline{\mathcal T_{\mathrm{TT}}}^{L^2}$.
In dimension three every coefficient is negative. In higher
dimensions, only finitely many eigenvalues lie at or below
$\lambda_*(n)$, while infinitely many lie above it. This proves
all the assertions.
head: environment

label: thm:negative-definite-3d
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For an eigentensor with eigenvalue $\lambda\geq3$,
\eqref{hd:main-mode}, \eqref{hd:fiber}, and
$\kappa_3(\lambda)\leq K_3=15\pi^2/64$ give
\[
 \mathcal H(S,S)
 \leq-\frac{\eta}{60V_0}(\lambda-2)\|S\|_{L^2}^2
 \leq-\frac{\eta}{240V_0}(1+\lambda)\|S\|_{L^2}^2.
\]
The last inequality is $\lambda-2\geq(1+\lambda)/4$ for $\lambda\geq3$.
Sum using \eqref{eq:full-spectral-hessian} to obtain
\eqref{eq:negative-definite-3d}.
head: environment

label: lem:constraint-coordinates
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:constraint-coordinates}
In the affine slice $\delta(g-g_0)=0$, the metrics with scalar curvature
$-6$ near $g_0$ admit a smooth $H^8$ parametrization
\[
 G(S)=g_0+S+\mathcal R w(S),\qquad S\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{TT}}^8,
 \qquad w(0)=0,\quad Dw(0)=0.
\]
Here $w(S)\in H^6$, and $\mathcal R:H^6\to H^8$ is a fixed bounded
linear operator. Every smooth metric sufficiently close to $g_0$ with
scalar curvature $-6$ is, after pullback by a diffeomorphism, of this
form. Its coordinate $S$ is small in $H^{22}$ when the original metric
is sufficiently close in the smooth topology.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $L=D\operatorname{Sc}_{g_0}$. Its formal adjoint on functions is
\[
 L^*f=\operatorname{Hess} f+(\Delta f)g_0+2fg_0.
\]
Diffeomorphism invariance of scalar curvature gives $\delta L^*f=0$.
Its trace is $2(\Delta+3)f$, and on divergence-free tensors
$LH=(\Delta+2)\operatorname{tr} H$. Thus
\[
 LL^*=2(\Delta+2)(\Delta+3),\qquad
 \mathcal R=L^*\bigl[2(\Delta+2)(\Delta+3)\bigr]^{-1}
\]
satisfies $L\mathcal R=\operatorname{Id}$ and
$\delta\mathcal R=0$. Elliptic estimates make $\mathcal R$ bounded
from $H^{r-2}$ to $H^r$. Every divergence-free tensor $H\in H^r$ decomposes as
\[
 H=S+\mathcal R LH,\qquad S=H-\mathcal R LH\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{TT}}^r.
\]
The equations $LS=0$ and $\delta S=0$ give
$(\Delta+2)\operatorname{tr} S=0$, hence $\operatorname{tr} S=0$.

The map
\[
 (S,w)\longmapsto\operatorname{Sc}(g_0+S+\mathcal R w)+6,
 \qquad \mathcal T_{\mathrm{TT}}^8\times H^6\longrightarrow H^6,
\]
is smooth on the open set of positive metrics. Its derivative in $w$
at zero is the identity. The Banach implicit function theorem gives
$w(S)$, and differentiation in a TT direction gives $Dw(0)=0$.
The decomposition above and uniqueness in that theorem show that
$G$ parametrizes all nearby constrained metrics in the affine slice.
The constructions at higher Sobolev regularity agree wherever both
are defined, by uniqueness.

The slice is obtained by solving
$\delta(\psi^*g-g_0)=0$ near $\psi=\operatorname{Id}$.
Its linearization in the vector field generating $\psi$ is
$X\mapsto\delta\mathcal L_Xg_0$. This elliptic operator has zero
kernel, as proved in Section~\ref{sec:constraint}. With $g$ in
$C^{25,1/2}$, the equation defines a $C^1$ map from vector fields in
$C^{24,1/2}$ to one-forms in $C^{22,1/2}$, and its linearization is an
isomorphism between these spaces. The implicit function theorem
therefore gives a nearby $\psi$, continuously depending on $g$.
The pullback is close in $C^{23,1/2}$, hence in $H^{22}$.
Since $H\mapsto H-\mathcal R LH$ is bounded on $H^{22}$, its TT
coordinate is also small in $H^{22}$. For smooth metrics, elliptic
regularity for this gauge equation gives a smooth diffeomorphism.
head: environment

label: lem:entropy-remainder
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We prove $C^3$ regularity in the $H^8$ topology.
On the fixed bundle $S_{g_0}M$, the geodesic vector field depends
smoothly on the metric, losing one spatial derivative. Structural
stability gives a positive H\"older time-change function $a_g$ whose
dependence on a $C^4$ vector field is $C^3$ with values in a fixed
H\"older space (see \cite{KKPW}*{Proposition~2.2 and its proof,
pp.~591--592}). Thus $g\mapsto a_g$ is $C^3$ on a sufficiently small
$C^{5,1/2}$ neighborhood. Normalize the time change so that its integral
on a closed $g_0$ orbit is the period of the corresponding $g$ orbit.
The entropy is determined by
\[
 \mathscr P_{g_0}(-h(g)a_g)=0,
\]
where $\mathscr P_{g_0}$ is the pressure of the fixed geodesic flow.
Pressure is analytic on this H\"older space, and its derivative in the
scalar variable $h$ is $-\int a_g\,d\mu$, which is strictly negative;
here $\mu$ is the equilibrium probability measure
(see \cite{KKPW}*{Proposition~2.1 and the proof of Theorem~2,
pp.~589--590 and~594}). The implicit function theorem makes
$g\mapsto h(g)$ a $C^3$ function on this neighborhood.
This is Fr\'echet differentiability, as specified on p.~594 of the cited paper.
All the metrics are negatively curved, so topological and volume
entropy coincide.

In dimension three, $H^8$ embeds continuously into $C^{5,1/2}$.
Composing with $G$ therefore makes $F$ a $C^3$ function on $\mathcal T_{\mathrm{TT}}^8$.
Here $DF(0)=0$ and $D^2F(0)=\mathcal H$, since $G(0)=g_0$ and
$DG(0)S=S$. Continuity of $D^3F$ bounds its operator norm on a sufficiently
small ball centered at zero. Taylor's formula on this ball gives
\[
 |F(S)-2-\tfrac12\mathcal H(S,S)|\leq C\|S\|_{H^8}^3.
\]
Sobolev interpolation, with $8=\tfrac23\cdot1+\tfrac13\cdot22$, gives
\[
 \|S\|_{H^8}^3\leq\|S\|_{H^1}^2\|S\|_{H^{22}},
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:uniform-remainder}.
head: environment

label: prop:constrained-local-maximum
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:constrained-local-maximum}
For all smooth metrics $g$ sufficiently close to $g_0$ with
$\operatorname{Sc}_g=-6$, one has $h(g)\leq2$. Equality holds precisely when
$g$ is a pullback of $g_0$ by a diffeomorphism.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:constraint-coordinates}, write $\psi^*g=G(S)$ with
$S$ small in $H^{22}$. Entropy is invariant under pullback.
Proposition~\ref{cor:coercive-3d} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:entropy-remainder} imply
\[
 h(g)-2\leq\left(-\frac {c_0}2+C\|S\|_{H^{22}}\right)\|S\|_{H^1}^2
 \leq-\frac {c_0}4\|S\|_{H^1}^2
\]
after shrinking the neighborhood. Equality forces $S=0$, hence
$\psi^*g=G(0)=g_0$. Conversely, pullbacks of $g_0$ have entropy $2$.
head: environment

label: prop:conformal-reduction
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:conformal-reduction}
For smooth metrics $g$ sufficiently close to $g_0$, there is a positive
function $u_g$ close to $1$ such that
\[
 \widehat g=u_g^4g,\qquad \operatorname{Sc}_{\widehat g}=-6.
\]
The assignment $g\mapsto\widehat g$ is continuous in the smooth topology
and fixes $g_0$. If $\operatorname{Sc}_g\geq-6$, then
\[
 u_g\leq1,\qquad \widehat g\leq g,\qquad h(g)\leq h(\widehat g).
\]
Consequently, Question~\ref{q:KSX-local-entropy} is equivalent to the
existence of a neighborhood of $g_0$ on which $h\leq2$ for metrics
in $\mathcal M_{-6}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $k\geq4$ and $0<\alpha<1$. The conformal scalar-curvature
formula reduces the normalization to
\[
 F(g,u):=8\Delta_g u+\operatorname{Sc}_g u+6u^5=0,
\]
where $\Delta_g$ is the nonnegative Laplacian. At $(g_0,1)$,
\[
 D_uF(g_0,1)=8(\Delta_{g_0}+3),
\]
an isomorphism from $C^{k,\alpha}$ to $C^{k-2,\alpha}$.
The implicit function theorem gives a unique solution near $1$,
depending continuously on $g$ in $C^{k,\alpha}$. It is positive after
shrinking the neighborhood. Elliptic regularity makes the solution
smooth for smooth $g$. Applying the same argument at higher regularity,
and using uniqueness to identify the solutions, gives continuity in
the smooth topology.

Suppose $\operatorname{Sc}_g\geq-6$. At a maximum point of $u=u_g$,
$\Delta_g u\geq0$, so
\[
 -6u^5=8\Delta_g u+\operatorname{Sc}_g u\geq-6u.
\]
Thus $u\leq1$ everywhere. To compare entropies, lift both metrics
to the universal cover. Since $\widehat g\leq g$, their balls satisfy
$B_g(x,R)\subset B_{\widehat g}(x,R)$. Compactness of $M$ gives
$dV_g\leq C\,dV_{\widehat g}$ for a constant independent of $R$.
Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{Vol}_g B_g(x,R)\leq C\operatorname{Vol}_{\widehat g}B_{\widehat g}(x,R).
\]
Taking logarithms, dividing by $R$, and passing to the limit proves
$h(g)\leq h(\widehat g)$. Finally, continuity of the normalization
allows its image to lie in any prescribed neighborhood of $g_0$.
Thus a bound on the constant-scalar-curvature metrics implies the
bound under $\operatorname{Sc}_g\geq-6$. The converse follows by restriction
to $\operatorname{Sc}_g=-6$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Shrink the neighborhood so that the conformal normalization
$\widehat g=u^4g$ in Proposition~\ref{prop:conformal-reduction} lies in
the neighborhood of Proposition~\ref{prop:constrained-local-maximum}.
If $\operatorname{Sc}_g\geq-6$, these propositions give
\[
 h(g)\leq h(\widehat g)\leq2.
\]
To determine equality, put $v=1-u\geq0$. The conformal equation gives
\[
 8\Delta_g v+6u(1+u+u^2+u^3)v=(\operatorname{Sc}_g+6)u\geq0.
\]
The zero-order coefficient is positive. Since $M$ is connected, the
strong maximum principle implies that either $v\equiv0$ or $v>0$
everywhere. In the latter case, compactness gives $\rho=\max_M u<1$.
Then $\widehat g\leq\rho^4g$, so metric comparison and entropy scaling
give
\[
 h(g)\leq\rho^2h(\widehat g)\leq2\rho^2<2.
\]
Thus $h(g)=2$ forces $u=1$, and the equality statement in
Proposition~\ref{prop:constrained-local-maximum} makes $g$ a pullback of
$g_0$. The converse follows from diffeomorphism invariance.
head: environment

label: rem:logic
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:logic}
Choose the neighborhood so that $C\|S\|_{H^{22}}<c_0/4$ after fixing
the gauge. By Lemma~\ref{lem:entropy-remainder}, the Taylor remainder
is then bounded by $(c_0/4)\|S\|_{H^1}^2$, uniformly for all $S$
in this neighborhood.

label: hd:bending-input
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{hd:bending-input}
For each $n\geq3$ there are closed oriented hyperbolic manifolds
$M=\Gamma\backslash\mathbb H^n$ with
\[
 H^1(\Gamma;\mathbb R^{n,1})\ne0,
\]
where $\Gamma$ acts through its standard hyperbolic holonomy.
Here $H^1$ denotes group cohomology with the indicated coefficients.
These examples can be obtained by bending along embedded totally geodesic
hypersurfaces, viewing the holonomy in $SO_0(n+1,1)$.
head: environment

label: hd:flat-bundle
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The flat bundle associated with the standard holonomy is
$E=TM\oplus\mathbb R$, with connection
\begin{equation*}
 D_X(Y,s)=(\nabla_XY+sX,\ X(s)+g_0(X,Y)).
\end{equation*}
The curvature $-1$ identity gives $D^2=0$, and $D$ preserves the
Lorentz form $|Y|^2-s^2$.  Since the universal cover of $M$ is
contractible, flat de Rham theory gives
\[
 H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;E)
 \simeq H^1(\Gamma;\mathbb R^{n,1}),
\]
where $H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;E)$ denotes the $D$-closed $E$-valued
one-forms modulo $D$-exact forms.  We identify endomorphisms with
two-tensors using $g_0$.  A symmetric Codazzi tensor
$A$ defines a closed form $(A,0)$; we prove that each cohomology
class has a unique such representative with $\operatorname{tr} A=0$.

Let $\alpha(X)=(A(X),b(X))$ be a closed form.
The scalar component of $D(b^\sharp,0)$ is $b$, so subtracting
this exact form gives a representative $(A,0)$, with $A$ renamed.
The scalar and tangent components of its closedness condition give
\[
 g_0(A(X),Y)=g_0(X,A(Y)),\qquad
 (\nabla_XA)(Y)=(\nabla_YA)(X).
\]
Thus $A$ is symmetric and Codazzi.  To remove its trace, observe that
\[
 D(\nabla f,-f)(X)=((\operatorname{Hess} f-f\operatorname{Id})(X),0).
\]
The trace of its tangent component is $-(\Delta+n)f$, since
$\Delta=-\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Hess}$ on functions.  Solve
$-(\Delta+n)f=\operatorname{tr} A$, using invertibility of $\Delta+n$ on the
closed manifold $M$.  Subtracting this exact form removes the trace.
The new representative is still closed and has scalar component zero,
so it is still symmetric and Codazzi.

To prove uniqueness, suppose a trace-free representative is exact:
$(A,0)=D(Y,s)$.  Its scalar component gives $Y=-\nabla s$,
so $A=-\operatorname{Hess} s+s\operatorname{Id}$.  Taking the trace gives
$(\Delta+n)s=0$, hence $s=0$ and $A=0$.
This proves the isomorphism.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose a nonzero trace-free Codazzi tensor $S^+$. Its Hessian is positive
by Corollary~\ref{hd:codazzi-sign}. Choose any TT eigentensor $S^-$
with eigenvalue greater than $\lambda_*(n)$; its Hessian is negative.
Lemma~\ref{lem:integrability} integrates both tensors to constrained curves.
Their first entropy variations vanish, and therefore
\[
 h(g_s^\pm)=n-1+\frac{s^2}{2}\mathcal H(S^\pm,S^\pm)+o(s^2).
\]
This gives the two strict inequalities for sufficiently small nonzero
$s$. Proposition~\ref{hd:bending-input} and
Theorem~\ref{hd:flat-bundle} provide such manifolds in every dimension
$n\geq4$. The curves are smooth and negatively curved near zero.
